# Data retention matrix

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:retention` from src/compliance/retention.ts. Do not edit by hand:
     tests/compliance/retention.test.ts fails when this file differs from the generator output. -->

This is the engineering record of what Lumi Noti stores, why, for how long and how it is removed
(spec 15 F237). Every period below is read from the code that enforces it. **It is not a privacy
policy and contains no legal conclusion.** Legal basis, controller or processor role, and any
regulatory retention period are to be decided by the operator. No formal security audit has been performed.

A test lists every table created by the migrations and fails if one is missing from the matrix, so a
new table cannot ship without a retention decision. It also checks that each removal mechanism named
below exists in the schema or the purge code.

## D1 stores

| Store | Data held | Purpose | Category | Personal data | Retention | Removed by | Exported in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | Name, email address, email-verified flag, optional image, timestamps. | Sign-in identity; shows who a workspace member is. | `account_identity` | direct | Until the account is deleted | account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | workspace and account. The workspace export lists each member name and email; the account export lists the full record. |
| `session` | Session token (a usable credential, AR-1), IP address, user agent, active workspace, timestamps. | Keeps a person signed in; the IP address and user agent help a person recognise a session. | `session_and_device` | direct | Until it expires (90 days), then removed at the next hourly pass | cron job `expired_auth_purge`; foreign-key cascade from `user`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | account. Metadata only (times, IP address, user agent). The token and the row id are never exported. |
| `account` | Sign-in method record: provider id, provider account id, password hash (email and password), OAuth token columns (unused by the current sign-in methods), timestamps. | Authenticates the person. | `authentication_credential` | direct | Until the account is deleted | foreign-key cascade from `user`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | account. Provider id and creation time only. The password hash and token columns are never exported. |
| `verification` | One-time verification and password-reset records (identifier, value, expiry). | Email verification and password reset. | `authentication_credential` | indirect | Until it expires (1 hour), then removed at the next hourly pass | cron job `expired_auth_purge` | neither. Short-lived security records; not exported. |
| `passkey` | Credential id, public key, signature counter, device type, transports, a user-chosen name. | Passwordless sign-in. | `authentication_credential` | direct | Until the account is deleted | foreign-key cascade from `user`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | account. Name, device type, backup flag, transports and creation time. The public key, credential id and counter are not exported. |
| `rate_limit` | Better Auth request counters keyed by caller and path (UNVERIFIED: the key can embed an IP address). | Limits sign-in, sign-up and reset requests. | `abuse_control_counter` | indirect | 1 day (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AGE_MS (src/pipeline/expired-records.ts)). Counted from the last request. | cron job `expired_auth_purge` | neither. Operational counter; not exported. |
| `member` | Which person belongs to which workspace, and their role. | Authorisation: decides what a person may do in a workspace. | `workspace_membership` | direct | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | foreign-key cascade from `user`; foreign-key cascade from `organization`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | workspace and account. Workspace export: name, email, role and joined date per member. Account export: the person own memberships. |
| `invitation` | Invitee email address, role, status, expiry, who invited them. | Lets a workspace admin invite a person. | `workspace_membership` | direct | 30 days (INVITATION_PURGE_AFTER_EXPIRY_MS (src/pipeline/expired-records.ts)). Counted from the invitation expiry, whatever its status (accepted, declined or expired). Removed by the hourly expired-auth pass (ADR 0044). | cron job `expired_auth_purge`; foreign-key cascade from `organization`; foreign-key cascade from `user`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | account. Invitations the person sent, without the invitee email address (a third party). |
| `organization` | Workspace name, slug, logo, free-form metadata. | The tenant itself. | `tenant_configuration` | indirect | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | workspace purge (organization delete) | workspace. Id and name. |
| `github_installations` | GitHub App installation id, the GitHub account login it is installed on, repository-selection mode, status. The access_token_ciphertext column exists but no code writes it. | Binds a verified GitHub installation to exactly one workspace (tenant resolution). | `tenant_configuration` | indirect | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | foreign-key cascade from `organization` | workspace |
| `github_installation_repositories` | Repository ids and full names (owner/name) the installation can see. Private repository names are customer-confidential. | Repository-scope enforcement and the repository picker. | `tenant_configuration` | none | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | foreign-key cascade from `github_installations`; workspace purge (via installation) | neither. Not in the workspace export today (a gap): the export lists installations, not their repositories. |
| `github_installation_tombstones` | GitHub installation id and App id of an installation that GitHub reported deleted, and when. | Stops a deleted installation from being bound again. | `platform_state` | none | No expiry. A tombstone that expired would let a deleted installation be bound again. | none. Numeric GitHub ids and a timestamp only; no workspace or person is referenced. | neither |
| `github_auth_states` | Hash of a single-use install/OAuth state, purpose, workspace id, user id, PKCE verifier, expiry, used-at. | Binds the GitHub install flow to the person and workspace that started it. | `authentication_credential` | indirect | Until it expires (10 minutes), then 1 day more | cron job `expired_auth_purge`; workspace purge (drained); foreign-key cascade from `organization`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | neither. Short-lived security records; not exported. |
| `integrations` (14 columns: configuration) | Integration settings, routing filters, noise settings, destination kind and host, and the id of the person who created it. | Routes events to destinations. | `tenant_configuration` | indirect | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | customer deletes the integration; workspace purge (tenant tables) | workspace. The creator id (created_by) is in neither export. |
| `integrations` (10 columns: sealed credentials) | Destination webhook URL and signing secret, sealed with a per-integration data key that is wrapped by a versioned key-encryption key (ADR 0004). | Lets the Worker deliver to the destination. | `tenant_credential_sealed` | none | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | customer deletes the integration; workspace purge (tenant tables) | neither. Sealed credentials are never exported, in any form. |
| `sources` (17 columns: configuration) | Source settings, the public endpoint id, counters, and the id of the person who created it. | Receives signed webhooks from a provider. | `tenant_configuration` | indirect | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | customer deletes the source; workspace purge (tenant tables); foreign-key cascade from `organization` | workspace |
| `sources` (6 columns: sealed credentials) | The per-source signing secret, sealed like integration credentials. | Verifies the signature of inbound webhooks. | `tenant_credential_sealed` | none | While the workspace exists; 7 days grace period after a deletion request | customer deletes the source; workspace purge (tenant tables) | neither. Sealed credentials are never exported, in any form. |
| `notification_outbox` | The rendered notification waiting to be sent: title, link, repository, the sender login, a short summary. Never the raw provider payload, never a credential. | Durable hand-off from ingress to the queue, and the source for manual redelivery. | `tenant_event_content` | indirect | 7 days (OUTBOX_RETENTION_MS (src/delivery/claim.ts)). Applies to invalid rows, and to rows of deliveries that were sent, accepted or suppressed (those cannot be replayed, so the row is no longer needed). Rows of dead-lettered and failed deliveries are kept with their delivery, because a manual replay re-reads them (src/delivery/redeliver.ts). Orphans, with no delivery left, go with the delivery retention (retention_purge). | cron job `outbox_reconcile`; cron job `retention_purge`; workspace purge (tenant tables) | neither. Notification content is workspace data and is not in the export today. |
| `deliveries` | Delivery ledger: ids, state, attempts, error codes (our own taxonomy), timestamps, a dedup key and a body hash. No notification text, no destination URL. | Answers "did you send this?"; drives retries, dead letters and redelivery. | `delivery_metadata` | none | DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS: default 90 days, allowed 30 days to 365 days | cron job `retention_purge`; workspace purge (tenant tables) | workspace. The most recent 2,000 rows. |
| `delivery_attempts` | One row per delivery attempt or wait: outcome, our own error code, a diagnostic code we minted, an HTTP status class, a retry delay in milliseconds. No notification text, no destination URL, no provider response. | Answers "what happened on each try?" in the delivery log. | `delivery_metadata` | none | DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS: default 90 days, allowed 30 days to 365 days | cron job `retention_purge`; workspace purge (tenant tables) | workspace. The most recent 2,000 rows. |

Only rows whose breaker is closed and that have been quiet for this long; an open breaker is state, not garbage. | cron job `retention_purge`; workspace purge (tenant tables) | neither |

Counted from release. A row that is still waiting is kept until it is released. Rows that failed to release are kept 30 days (FAILED_RETENTION_MS). | cron job `noise_purge`; customer deletes the integration; workspace purge (tenant tables) | neither |

## Legal basis (to be completed by the operator)

Every row has a `legalBasis` and a `controllerRole` field in `src/compliance/retention.ts`, set to "to be decided by the operator".
This repository takes no position on them. The operator must decide, per row, why the data may be
processed and in which role, and record it with qualified advice before the documents are shown to
customers.

| `github_auth_states` | to be decided by the operator | to be decided by the operator |

## Stores outside D1

Not machine-checked. The retention of these is set by Cloudflare or by account configuration, not by this code.

| Store | Holds | Retention | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare D1 Time Travel | Point-in-time history of the whole database, including rows we have deleted. | Cloudflare-managed. docs/SECURITY.md records up to 30 days (read 2026-10-13); not re-verified for this document. | Cloudflare. We cannot shorten it, so a deletion is not erasure from this history until the window has passed. |
| Cloudflare Queues (deliveries and dead letters) | Queue messages carry ids and display text, never a credential (F173). | Cloudflare-managed. Spec 15 F237 records up to 14 days on the Paid plan; not re-verified for this document. | Cloudflare. |
| Workers logs | Redacted operational log lines: correlation id, counts, error categories. No payloads, URLs or tokens by design (src/platform/redact.ts). | Retention is a Cloudflare account setting that this repository does not configure: to be decided by the operator. | Cloudflare account configuration. |
| Cloudflare Email Sending | Verification, password-reset and invitation emails sent to a person (recipient address and the one-time link). | Cloudflare-managed delivery records: to be decided by the operator. | Cloudflare. |

## Not stored (spec rows that do not apply)

The spec retention table (docs/specs/15 F237) names these. The code does not store them, so no period applies.

| Spec row | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| F237: "Raw provider payload", 7 days | Not stored. The provider request body is verified and parsed for the request and is not written to D1 or to a queue message. What is kept is the rendered notification (notification_outbox, see its row) and routing metadata, so the payload period does not apply. |
| F237: "Normalized envelope", same as the payload | The event as delivered is the rendered notification in notification_outbox, so its period is that row period, not the payload period. |
| F237: "semantic_dedup", 7 days | No such table exists. Repeat events are recognised by event_dedup (the transport key) alone; an object-level dedup would need a decision and a table first. |

## Deletion and its limits

- **Workspace deletion** is two-phase: integrations are disabled at once, and a cron purge removes every
  tenant row and the workspace after the grace period shown above (`src/pipeline/purge.ts`). Deleting an
  integration or source row destroys its wrapped data key, so sealed credentials cannot be opened afterwards.
- **Account erasure** (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) deletes the person and everything that cascades from them.
  It refuses (409) while the person is the only admin of a workspace. See `docs/DSAR.md`.
- **Not erasure:** D1 Time Travel keeps point-in-time history for a period set by Cloudflare, so a deleted row
  can still exist in that history until the window passes (AR-6). Queues and logs are likewise Cloudflare-retained.
- Tables that carry an `organization_id` but are deliberately not removed by the workspace purge: `workspace_deletions`.

## Known gaps

- `legacy_orphaned_rows`: Nothing drops it. The operator reviews it after applying migration 0026 and runs DROP TABLE legacy_orphaned_rows (docs/RUNBOOK.md).
- `auth_users`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_orgs`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_memberships`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_tokens`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_invites`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- The expiry-based purge (`expired_auth_purge`) runs once an hour. `github_auth_states` has an index on its expiry (migration 0010);
  `session`, `verification` and `rate_limit` do not, so those scans read the whole table. Acceptable at current volume; add an index if they grow.
  A sanity guard aborts the pass, and logs `expired_purge_aborted`, if an expiry looks like seconds instead of milliseconds or more than half of a large `session` table would go.
- Accounts whose email was never verified are not purged by any job, and they cannot use `DELETE /api/workspace/me` (it needs a verified session). Only an operator can remove them (`RUNBOOK.md`, "Data-subject requests").
- Audit rows are append-only and keep the actor id, IP address and user agent after the actor is erased, until the audit retention.
- The workspace export does not include notification content (`notification_outbox`, `held_events`) or repository lists.

## Notes per store

- `user`: Accounts whose email was never verified are not purged by any job and cannot use the erasure route (it needs a verified session); they stay until an operator deletes them (gap).
- `session`: A session is usable until 30 days after its last refresh (refreshed at most daily) and never beyond 90 days after sign-in (SESSION_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS and SESSION_ABSOLUTE_SECONDS, ADR 0030). The row is removed by the first of the two. The 90-day figure in the table is that outer bound, not the idle period. The person can list and end their sessions (`/api/workspace/me/sessions`).
- `verification`: Each record expires after its explicit lifetime, one hour for email verification and one hour for password reset (src/auth/session-policy.ts, ADR 0030), and is removed by the hourly pass after that. Rows still valid at the time of an account deletion survive until they expire.
- `member`: A database trigger refuses to remove the last admin of a workspace outside a started purge.
- `invitation`: Erasing an account hands the pending invitations the person sent to another admin of the same workspace, so the invitee can still accept; sent invitations that are not pending (accepted, declined, expired) go with the cascade on the inviter. Invitations addressed TO the erased email address are deleted. A person whose email is not yet verified cannot use the erasure route (gap).
- `integrations` (integrations_credentials): Deleting the row destroys the wrapped data key, so a copy of the ciphertext (for example in a Time Travel restore) cannot be opened without that row.
- `deliveries`: Only terminal deliveries are purged; a dead-lettered row is kept until both its creation and its dead-lettering are older than the cutoff. The spec table (docs/specs/15 F237) once said the ledger lasts as long as the workspace; the period is 90 days by default, set by ADR 0011, and that is the enforced value (ADR 0044).
- `delivery_attempts`: Deleted with the delivery it belongs to; a delivery is only purged once none remain.
- `audit_events`: Erasing an account does not rewrite these rows: a database trigger refuses every UPDATE (migration 0008). They keep the opaque actor id, the IP address and the user agent until the audit retention above, which the operator must weigh against the erasure obligation.
